question: Your Claude Agent SDK tool helps engineers understand a legacy system. For one task, Claude first calls Glob to list configuration files, then chooses which files to open with Read, and later decides whether to run Bash. Your team is designing how the agentic loop handles each tool's output before it sends the next request to Claude. Which design lets Claude base each next action on everything the tools have returned so far?

options.text: Append Claude's tool_use response and then the tool output as a tool result to the existing conversation history, keeping every earlier turn.
options.reason: The guide says tool results are appended to the conversation history so the model can reason about the next action with the new information.

options.text: Return only a short status such as "Glob succeeded" as the tool result, and keep the full output in the loop's own log file.
options.reason: Claude never sees the actual file list. The guide requires the tool results themselves to be added to the context so that Claude can incorporate the new information.

options.text: Rebuild the request on each iteration from the original user message plus only the newest tool result, dropping earlier results to keep the context window small.
options.reason: Dropping earlier results removes them from the conversation history. Claude can then no longer use the Glob list when it chooses which files to Read or whether to run Bash.

options.text: Collect every tool output in a local variable and send all of them to Claude together after the loop ends with stop_reason "end_turn".
options.reason: The guide says tool results are returned between iterations for the next request. Holding them until the end means Claude chooses each next tool without seeing what the earlier tools returned.
